To be honest I started posting a few of these stories on /b/ but I really wanted some more artistic freedom (read: no greentext), so this seems to be a good place to go. Anyways, I was diagnosed with ADHD when I was seven, and apparently that was enough for the school to classify me as a tard. Even though I was in normal classes, I was, for all intents and purposes, treated like a tard in middle school. I had special tard shit that I had to go to, was put in a "tard study hall", but other than that I was treated completely normally. On one side, there were people such as Captain Ham, Majin Buu, and Trenchcoat Guy. On the other side was people like Hulk and Puck. Naturally, some had more severe disabilities from the others, but despite that, were cooler than other "less disabled" tards. However, the first encounter in my middle school would be the most vivid, most memorable, and one of the most recurring tards in my life, Todd. Here are all of my experiences with this kid, good and bad.

I went to a very small elementary school in Illinois. Out of the ~200 kids there, you could only call a few kids actual tards, and even then they were at worst mid-functioning autistics. In fact, out of the 30 kids in my grade, there was me, my friend Puck (another ADHD kid, but with absolutely no filter whatsoever. also a huge Blackhawks fan and one of the few kids in my town to stick with them before Toews and Kane came along), and GB (mid-functioning, mostly played GameBoy all class). Down Syndrome was just something I heard in books and TV, and the only experience with someone who was a tard was an integration program. After that, we graduated to middle school. All the kids from my town and two other towns over just got lumped into the one large town near us.

To give you an idea of the structure, they split the 1500 kids into 3 grades of 500. From there they split into 5 groups. Each group has its own smaller TardHQ, its own wranglers, and its own head wrangler. So here I go over to the school for my homeroom assignment, and it's fucking huge. The lobby's the width of my entire elementary school. So I get there and there's one other kid named Cheech getting his assignments. Great, a few kids in my town are in my group so I'm not alone. Turns out the kid and I have the same homeroom too. We start shooting the shit, and he turns out to be a bro. Then, as he's looking down the list of people we have, he gets this look of dread on his face.

“Oh shoot!”

“What?”

“Todd's in our homeroom! He's crazy!”

Ma Dukes just tells me to ignore it and not to listen to rumors. To be honest I forget the kid's name by the time I get on my bus. College Dropout's playing on my iPod as I hop on the bus. It takes an hour to get there, but I've got friends to suffer with, so we're all suffering together, talking to pass the time. After waiting in the warmth to go in, I wander into homeroom for the first time and aimlessly look for my seat. Cheech says hi, I say hi to his friends, and introduce myself. Then I get to the next table with an open seat. Two girls are talking to each other and a fat, greasy kid's sitting there chilling, and on the notecard in front of the open seat is the name Jeff. I want to make more friends, so I sit down and first introduce myself to the two girls. They're keeping to themselves, so I turn to the one guy there and introduce myself to him, despite the fact that he smells a little off.

“HIYJUFF I'M TODD!”

tl;dr: After going to a really small school and not having any experiences with tards, I meet a kid who my friend thinks is crazy. He looks unkempt but completely unassuming, but I still decide to make friends with him. There's a lot more to come.
